title: Resilient on-call playbook for gradual region failover and priority-based load shedding
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Create a tested, automation-first on-call playbook that enables safe, progressive multi-region failover and priority-based load shedding with tuned alerting to reduce noisy pages. The playbook must: 1) define SLO-aware thresholds for circuit breakers and region evacuation; 2) implement progressive traffic reweighting and prefix/KV cache warming steps; 3) include automated remediation steps (runbook-runner playbooks) for common failure modes; and 4) tune alert signal scoring so on-call only pages for high-fidelity incidents.

Why this work: Recent multi-region spikes caused flurry of pages and adhoc manual cutovers that increased downtime and customer-impact. We need a repeatable, minimally-invasive failover pattern that preserves P50 latency SLAs for critical routes while protecting capacity for enterprise customers during overloads.

Scope: API routing, serving runtime circuit breakers, traffic-controller runbooks, PagerDuty/Slack integration, and observability dashboards (SLO, latency, error budget burn). Excludes: changes to underlying scheduler (separate RFC).

Key design decisions so far: 1) Use three-tier priority buckets (critical, interactive, background) per-customer-route so load shedding favors lower-priority work. 2) Progressive region cutover will use a 4-step sequence: sample floodgate (1-2% traffic), warm cache (5-10%), steady reweight (25-50%), full cutover. Each step has SLO checks and automatic rollback on regression. 3) Circuit breaker trips on combined token-based error rate with hysteresis window (30s open, 5m half-open probe with exponential backoff). 4) Alerting uses a composite signal: SLO burn rate + region-specific error slope + internal health score; only above a calculated confidence threshold do we page.

Success criteria: reduce on-call pages for region overloads by 60% while maintaining >=99.5% P50 latency for critical routes during gradual failovers; fully automated runbook for the top 3 failure classes (regional GPU OOM, routing config drift, KV cache cold-start).
tasks: Finalize SLO thresholds and burn-rate policies for critical/interact/background buckets
Define circuit breaker parameters and hysteresis probing algorithm
Implement traffic-controller progressive reweight flow (k8s operator + API)
Create runbook-runner playbooks for automated cutover/warmup/rollback
Add composite alert scoring and update PagerDuty escalation policies
Author observability dashboards and synthetic canaries for pre-cutover validation
Run tabletop drills and one staged failover to validate rolling steps
updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created. Initial architects: Aisha, Lucas, Priya. Collected incident logs from 2026-02-20 regional surge.
2026-03-11: Design review — agreed on three-tier priority buckets and progressive reweight strategy. Action: eng to prototype traffic-controller API with staged reweight endpoint (Lucas).

2026-03-12: Prototype: traffic-controller supports 'sample' and 'warm' phases via /v1/traffic/reweight. Basic warmup handshake implemented; cache-warm webhook fires to region agents. PR: github.com/redwood/traffic-controller/pull/412 (prototype).

2026-03-13: Alert tuning spike: implemented composite signal in staging (slo_burn > 4x AND error_slope > 0.02 in 1m). Reduced pages in staging by 70%. Need to tune thresholds for low-traffic customers to avoid silent failures.
2026-03-14: Runbook automation: PoC runbook-runner playbook to perform warmup and 25% reweight deployed to staging. Playbook includes automatic rollback on SLO regressions (links below).
acceptance_criteria: Automated progressive cutover flow exists and is callable from runbook-runner or via console UI
Two synthetic canaries detect regression within 30s during each step and trigger auto-rollback
PagerDuty only pages when composite signal confidence > 0.9; for confidence 0.6-0.9 create Slack channel alert but do not page
Post-drill metrics: pages for region overload incidents reduced by >=60% across three simulated drills
Playbook documented in Confluence and approved by SRE and Product Security
